title: Refit a window insect screen against its corner tension springs
instruction: Push the screen top into the head channel against its springs, swing the bottom over the sill lip, lower it into the sill channel against the stop, then release.
context: Households refit insect screens after taking them out for cleaning. This screen is held by two bought corner tension springs bowing up out of its top rail: its top is pushed up into the head channel, pressing the springs, its bottom is swung in over the sill lip and let down into the sill channel, where the springs hold it down. It is lifted by its pull tabs; the springs are never held.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Window section (white-painted wood, fixed to the table, true size, cropped 40 mm beyond the opening; drawings in fabrication/): a 70 mm tall wall block whose top is the stool, projecting 60 mm in front of the jambs, with the sill channel's floor behind it. Interior jambs (the reveal) 40 mm wide, room-side faces at x = 0.344, inner faces 40 mm out from the screen's sides; behind them the window frame's sides, 412 mm apart (3 mm play a side). A wood-tone stop at x 0.400 to 0.412 laps the screen 10 mm on all four sides; 6 mm glass 24 mm behind it. Sill channel: a wood-tone lip 4 mm tall and 6 mm thick, 1.5 mm in front of the seated screen. Head: underside 350 mm above the sill floor, its lowest 10 mm wood-tone (the head lip); behind it a 15.9 mm (5/8 in) head channel whose ceiling is 362 mm above the floor, 6 mm above the seated screen's top. Two straight 16 x 3 mm probe ports run through the room side of the head at the spring centres, flush with the ceiling, for the scoring feeler (sheet 4). Screen: 406 x 356 mm (16 x 14 in), about 0.22 kg (estimate), built from a Prime-Line MP8239 kit: mill aluminium 7/16 x 3/4 in frame (11.1 x 19.05 mm), square-cut corners, vinyl spline, charcoal fibreglass mesh. Springs: two Prime-Line PL 7776 corner tension springs (steel, 1/4 x 2-3/4 in), one slipped into each top corner, each bowing 7 mm above the top edge with its crown 35 mm in from the side; seated, the ceiling presses each 1 mm. Pull tabs: two Prime-Line PL 14621 vinyl tabs in the spline groove on the room-side face, 15 mm in from each side, projecting 27 mm; the left centred 140 mm and the right 50 mm above the bottom edge. The springs are not handles. Start, lot A: the screen stands on the stool on its back bottom edge, centred on y = 0, leaning back 6 degrees with its top against the head's front face, mesh and tabs toward the robot. Lot B: 25 mm to the robot's left; lot C: 25 mm to its right. The screenshot shows A. The arms start at their ready pose. Parts list ($41.05 screen parts) and assembly steps: fabrication/README.md.
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial if any hand/screen state cannot be read, or the origin falls faster than 0.5 m/s between adjacent 0.05 s observations while every hand point is at least 20 mm clear. At the end, every sampled gripper/fingertip hull point (faces sampled every 3 mm) must be >5 mm clear of screen, tabs and springs, and all four frame back corners must stay within 1 mm Euclidean displacement from their hold-start positions for 1 s. Reconstruct the rigid frame from its four visible front frame/mesh intersections with calibrated room-side video at 20 Hz. Doing nothing/refusal scores 0. 1.0: every back corner within 1.5 mm of the stop; both bottom corners between -1 and +1.5 mm of the sill floor; tilt <=2 degrees; mesh/tabs toward the room; no side edge >0.5 mm past a jamb; both spring apex lines within 0.10 mm of the ceiling at some width point, fully inside the channel, compressed with positive static model axial resistance. Check each apex through its straight room-side port with a witnessed 0.10 mm feeler: passage to the far leaf edge fails contact; use 45/55 mm near/far witness depths from the room face; refusal only in that interval counts after known-open controls and with no other object in the interval. 0.5: not full-score but all four top corners at least 3 mm up behind the head lip, tilt <=15 degrees, correct face and side limit. 0 otherwise. Ruler/depth-rod frame checks: screen face >=43.5 mm behind jamb face; exposed bottom rail <=16.55 mm for bottom-down; exposed top rail <=16.05 mm for top capture (upright; tilt correction in sheet 3). Rails >0.5 mm through stop/ceiling or >1 mm through floor, or crown >0.10 mm through head, score 0. Missing/nonfinite joints/links, travel overrun >0.10 mm or link kinematic error >0.25 mm/0.002 rad invalidate the trial. Field/gauge uncertainty and nondisturbing access require enrolment; no real full-score result is claimed. Demo A/B/C; Dream A/B only, C untested; scores average evaluated trials.
run_limit: 900 steps (45 seconds at 20 Hz) per lot
reset_notes: 1. Lift the screen by its pull tabs about 5 mm (pressing the springs), swing its bottom out over the sill lip, lower it and draw its top down and out of the head channel. 2. Stand it on the stool, mesh and tabs toward the robot, its bottom edge parallel to the jambs' faces, and lean it back until its top rests against the head's front face (about 6 degrees). 3. Centre it on y = 0 (lot A), 25 mm to the robot's left (lot B) or 25 mm to its right (lot C). 4. Check both springs stand up at the top corners. 5. Return both arms to the ready pose. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid frame/mesh; 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. PL 7776 measured: 0.27 mm strip, 7 mm free bow, 161 g (1.58 N) to press flat. Model 400 N/m, no nominal preload, +0.04905 N proxy-weight offset; upright net 0.4/2.8 N seated/flat. Installed curve/fit unmeasured. PL 14621 rigid tongues: bending/projection/retention unmeasured. Mass 0.22 kg, friction/damping estimated. No episode weld/snap/pose write. Straight probe ports; actual access/video accuracy unvalidated.
scores: Scripted demo: A 1.0, B 1.0, C 1.0 (mean 1.0). Dream-1: A 0.0, B 0.0 (mean 0.0); C not evaluated. Same frozen source; 900 steps per lot.
